newsitem.title: USA: Amer International wins bidding for Golden Eagle.
newsitem.headline: Amer International wins bidding for Golden Eagle.

text.p: American International Group Inc said it has been informed by the California Insurance Commissioner that it has won the bidding for Golden Eagle Insurance Co.
The company said it has begun working with the commissioner and his staff in preparation for taking over Golden Eagle.
It said it intends to establish a new company, to be named San Diego Casualty Co, to carry on the business.
An order from the California superior court is expected soon, American International said, as any delay would be detrimental to policyholders, employees and producers.
Golden Eagle, one of the largest writers of workers compensation insurance in California, was seized by the department of insurance in late January because of allegations of a reserve shortfall.

California insurance commissioner Chuck Quackenbush quickly announced a rehabilitation plan backed by Zurich Centre Group and Insurance Partners LP, but then changed course and opened up bidding for the business.

At that time, Quackenbush said that an increasing number of parties expressing an interest in the transaction made it necessary to establish a standardized process for bidders to submit their proposals.
American International did not disclose the terms of its bid, but said it was pleased to have won and looks forward to building this business in the future.
Golden Eagle wrote about $400 million of workers compensation and $300 million of property-casualty business in 1996.
American International said it intends to retain the employees necessary to conduct the business going forward and to keep the company's headquarters in San Diego.
American International also said it intends to enhance relationships with policyholders, agents and brokers.
"A key attraction of this transaction to AIG is the special relationship that has existed in the past between Golden Eagle and its producers," American International said in a statement.
